coverage.row: Acceptance 1: Readable.pipe(process.stdout|stderr), with no options or {end:true}, never calls end(); the stream stays writable after the source ends; a node -e program exits 0 with Node's stdout/stderr

Acceptance 2: vitest forks-pool shape — fork(entry, [], {stdio:'pipe'}) with child.stdout/stderr.pipe(process.stdout/stderr) — leaves both parent streams writable after the child closes; the parent's later lines print

Parity 1: stream/pipe-process-stdio.case (seeded) — 'a' / stdout still writable with listener deltas 0 / stderr {end:true} not ended / fd-1 lookalike finished / Writable behind a reassigned globalThis.process finished
Parity 2: stream/pipe-process-stdio-end-calls — Readable.pipe(process.stdout|stderr) end calls 0; pipeline(src, process.stdout|stderr) end calls 1
Parity 3: stream/pipe-process-stdio-exit (node-cli-eval, kernel Worker) — stdout/stderr 'piped to X\nX still writable\n', code 0 per launch
Parity 4: child_process/fork-stdout-pipe-process-stdio (child-worker) — 'child stdout line' / 'child closed 0; parent stdout still writable'

Fault matrix: poisoned-cache × pipe() inside a same-realm child — the parent's later require('node:process') is still its own process (=== process, pid, exitCode writes) and its pipe(process.stdout) stays exempt; carrier same-realm-child-pipe-parent-process (seeded)
